definition: In this packet, mutilation refers specifically to female genital mutilation/cutting, a culturally traditional practice that some people support or reject and that may be discussed in relation to having it performed by medical personnel. The packet does not provide enough information to define mutilation more broadly beyond this specific context.

reasons: The packet supports discussion of female genital mutilation/cutting (FGM/C) and its medicalization, but it does not establish the standalone term “mutilation” as specifically referring to FGM/C in this source.

The definition adds a restrictive sense statement about what the packet does not define more broadly; that meta-claim is not supported by the packet itself and is not a dictionary definition of the term.

The definition claims the packet “does not provide enough information to define mutilation more broadly beyond this specific context,” but the packet text does not explicitly address whether “mutilation” has other meanings or whether broader definition is possible; this is unsupported.

The definition states “mutilation refers specifically to female genital mutilation/cutting (FGM/C), a culturally traditional practice…”. While the packet discusses FGM/C and references “traditional cultural values,” it does not explicitly define FGM/C (or “mutilation”) as “a culturally traditional practice,” so that characterization is not directly supported.
